The '''''Corona''-class armed frigate''' was a saucer-shaped [[Starship/Legends|craft]] manufactured by [[Haor Chall Engineering/Legends|Haor Chall Engineering]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="GAW" /><ref name="VGUB">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Visual Guide: Ultimate Battles]]''</ref> It was based on an ancient [[Surronian cruiser]] design.

==Characteristics==
[[File:CoronaUnderside-DC.png|thumb|left|200px|The underside of a ''Corona''-class frigate]]
It was produced by [[Haor Chall Engineering/Legends|Haor Chall Engineering]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The ship proved to be unfit as a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Starship/Legends|ship]] for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|CIS]]. Haor Chall cancelled the production and sold the remaining ships to investors and other people who were interested in buying one. During the Clone Wars they were considered antiquities, and collectors paid many [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for these vessels.<ref name="VGUB" />

The vessel rotated while in flight, which was its main source of propulsion.<ref name="VGUB" /> As such, they also gave off a distinct humming sound while in flight. They had enough room for a [[Flarestar-class attack shuttle/Legends|''Flarestar''-class Weequay ships]], which could be launched from the center of its ventral superstructure.<ref name="DC" />

The craft was capable of landing on planetary surfaces and had eight landing legs. The eighth doubled as a boarding ramp.<ref name="DC" />

==History==
<div style="float:right">[[File:Weequay_saucer_landed.png|thumb|left|200px|Weequay pirate ship landed on [[Vanqor/Legends|Vanqor]].]]</div>
The pirate band of [[Hondo Ohnaka/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka]] used such a [[Acushnet/Legends|ship]] to carry out their raids. Ohnaka confiscated the ship from a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] collector in [[Farana (region)/Legends|Farana]] along with several ''Flarestar''-class Weequay ships.<ref name="VGUB" /> They landed on [[Vanqor/Legends|Vanqor]] during [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] hunt for [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], and scavenged the Count's [[Punworcca 116-class interstellar sloop/Legends|''Punworcca 116''-class interstellar sloop]]. Ohnaka offered the Count passage to [[Florrum/Legends|Florrum]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] six [[Parsec/Legends|parsecs]] away. Dooku accepted the offer to travel with them in the ship to [[Hondo's complex/Legends|their base]] on Florrum.<ref name="DC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ship design is a nod to the flying saucers popular in 1950s sci-fi films, with ''The Earth vs. The Flying Saucers'' being cited as an example. The writers admitted that since at least [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], they had wanted to try out a design for flying saucers as either Trade Federation craft or, more recently, as [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanean]] vessels, but they never got a chance to implement it until "[[Dooku Captured]]."<ref name="EG:DC">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode011.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Dooku Captured}}</ref>

The craft was first named a "Surronian cruiser" by [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Visual Guide: Ultimate Battles|''The Clone Wars: Visual Guide Ultimate Battles'']], but in ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' it was named a "''Corona''-class armed frigate." The publication ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]'' later established that the ''Corona''-class was a different starship than the [[Surronian cruiser]].
